scope: Selected verified surface artifacts and landing sites for the first atlas release; not an exhaustive inventory. Orbiting spacecraft are cataloged separately.

spatialContract.moon: Planetocentric Mean Earth/Polar Axis, DE421, east-positive 0–360 degrees for NASA NSSDCA lunar table coordinates.
spatialContract.mars: Planetocentric east-positive 0–360 degrees for specified Mars entries. Historical geodetic/cartographic figures are not silently substituted.
spatialContract.roverRule: A landing-site marker is not a moving rover’s current or final position. A rover without a verified final coordinate remains a named-area record without a pin.

objects.name: Ingenuity helicopter
objects.locationType: named area only; no object-level pin
objects.precisionNote: NASA identifies Valinor Hills in Neretva Vallis as the final-airfield area after Flight 72 on Jan. 18, 2024. NASA's published images do not give a verified coordinate for the helicopter; no point is plotted.

objects.name: Perseverance descent stage (sky crane)
objects.locationType: orbital-imaged debris; no verified object-level coordinate
objects.precisionNote: NASA's MRO image identifies the descent stage crash debris as a dark V-shaped pattern a safe distance from the rover. Published source verifies the relative site, but not a coordinate suitable for an object pin.

objects.name: Perseverance backshell and parachute
objects.locationType: orbital- and aerial-imaged debris; no verified object-level coordinate
objects.precisionNote: NASA confirms the backshell and parachute on the surface and documents the backshell from Ingenuity Flight 26. The source does not provide a coordinate; no point is plotted.

objects.name: Perseverance heat shield
objects.locationType: orbital-imaged debris; no verified object-level coordinate
objects.precisionNote: NASA's MRO image labels the heat-shield location in the landing debris field. No verified coordinate is supplied in the source, so no point is plotted.
